raw_comment:
What do you notice?

I noticed that areas affected by drought often happen to be states which produce a significant amount of America's food. A brief Google search showed the following states as the 10 biggest producers of food, in order: California, Iowa, Nebraska, Texas, Illinois, Minnesota, Kansas, Indiana, North Carolina, and Missouri.
Of those 10 high-volume food producing states, 5/10 of them experienced at least "extreme" drought, and 9/10 of them experienced at least "severe" drought. I wonder how these drought circumstances interact with the states' agriculture/irrigation. 

Even though Florida was not really affected by the drought conditions, to my knowledge, we import most of our food from other states. The drought conditions elsewhere could definitely affect prices in the grocery stores.

"United States Experience Harsh Drought Conditions in Late October"
